sections: 11.1.3 Namespace Nodes for Literal Result Elements
5 XML Output Method: reconstructed-tree namespace rules
6.1 Namespace Scoping: prefix undeclaration and subsequent rebinding

decision: Nearest namespace declarations and XML 1.1 undeclaration metadata both terminate ancestor lookup for their prefix. A deeper explicit rebinding remains effective.
Literal-result attribute namespace hints must use the same undeclaration-aware bindings, rather than resurrect an ancestor binding through LINQ-to-XML lookup.

Namespace fixup must remove obsolete undeclaration markers when the final element actually binds that prefix. Synthetic inheritance-barrier markers cannot hide the element's own binding from raw XDM namespace queries; missing-prefix markers remain effective.

Use the existing XmlWriter route with redundant identical namespace declarations omitted. Preserve genuine rebinding and default namespace resets. This is a serialization policy choice, not a claim that XML 1.0 universally prohibits redundant declarations.
Keep raw XDM namespace state separate from XML 1.0 reconstructed namespace state: XML 1.0 serialization cannot undeclare a nonempty prefix and may reconstruct additional bindings.
scope: No fixture edits, skip admissions, new schema coverage or standalone gate promotion. Preserve PR474 and all historical qualification receipts.
